chunks: And by this chain, from Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) who said:

He made the wergild of the foetus one hundred Dinars, and made the man's semen up to the stage it becomes a foetus into five segments. So if it is a foetus before the spirit enters it, it is one hundred Dinars. And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created man from an extract, which is the seed. So this is one segment. Then a clot, so it is two segments. Then a lump, so it is three segments. Then bones, so it is four segments. Then it is clothed with flesh, so at that time the foetus is complete, and its five segments are complete, being one hundred Dinars. And the one hundred Dinars are five segments: so for the seed is one-fifth of the hundred, twenty Dinars; and for the clot is two-fifths of the hundred, forty Dinars; and for the lump is three-fifths of the hundred, sixty Dinars; and for the bones is four-fifths of the hundred, eighty Dinars. So when the flesh covers it, it becomes one hundred Dinars complete.

So when another creation prevails in it, which is the spirit, then at that time it is a soul, and its wergild is one thousand Dinars complete if it is a male; and if it is a female, it is five hundred Dinars. And if a woman is killed while pregnant, and the foetus is complete and has not miscarried, and it is not known whether it is male or female, and it is not known whether it died after her or before her, then its wergild is two halves: half the wergild of the male and half the wergild of the female. And the wergild of the woman is complete after that, and that is six segments from the foetus.

And he (peace be upon him) issued a verdict regarding the semen of the man which flows out from his bride, so the water is isolated from her, and that is not returned, being half of the fifth of the hundred, ten Dinars; and when it is poured from her, it is twenty Dinars.

And he judged regarding the wergild of the injuries of the foetus from the accounting of the hundred, based on what it is, from the injury of the male and the female, the man and the woman complete. And he made for it in retaliation for its injury and its blood money according to the measure of its wergild, which is one hundred Dinars.
ai.seo_question: What is the wergild of a foetus at different stages of development in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) delineates a precise embryological taxonomy, linking the gradual increase in the foetus's blood money (diyah) from 20 to 100 dinars to the stages of nutfah, alaqah, and mudghah, culminating in the full 1,000 dinar compensation upon the entry of the soul (nafkh al-ruh). This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the concept of 'graduated personhood' and provides the legal basis for qisas (retaliation) and diyah calculations in cases of uncertain foetal gender or timing of death. The text reflects the integration of observed biological development with metaphysical spiritual reality, a key theme in Usuli fiqh.
